body: Decision card v1 for Automotive Axles Ltd. Rule output: size 0: blocked by Expected value vs hurdle (EV 1.40x anchored (raw 1.49x) vs hurdle 1.76x → below hurdle → size 0). Thesis: Method-test thesis: Automotive Axles is cheap only on peak-cycle earnings (12.9x trailing, 25.8x 10-year normalised EPS); over 5 years it compounds roughly with the M&HCV cycle at a through-cycle ROIC ~15-18% while its parent (Cummins/Meritor) takes ~4.5% of sales as a technical fee under an annually renewed agreement, so the 5-year outcome is driven by cycle position in FY31-32 and the exit multiple, not by a mispricing. Variant view: Market (reverse DCF and temperature): at Rs 1,776 the stock is at 12.9x trailing EPS, 8.1x EV/EBITDA net of Rs 394 cr cash, the lowest P/E on the highest earnings in its 11-year history; the market is pricing a cyclical peak (record FY27 M&HCV volume of 500k+ guided, a regulatory pre-buy to April 2027, capacity nearly full at a Rs 2,650 cr annualised run-rate). Our view: we largely AGREE that it is cheap for a reason, so there is no claimable mispricing. On 10-year normalised EPS (Rs 69) the P/E is 25.8x (warm vs own history); the last cycle took revenue -53% and EPS -81% (FY19-21) and the price -80% peak to trough. What we found that the market may be MIS-weighting, in both directions: (1, negative) like-for-like FY26 revenue was roughly flat while the industry grew ~16% - the reported +4.8% is mostly the gross-up from selling direct to OEMs at OEM prices since 1-Apr-2025 (materials fell 71.0% -> 67.5% of revenue, other expenses rose 11.7% -> 14.3% with the new Rs 97.5 cr technical fee) - so content/share per industry vehicle has lagged; (2, negative) the parent take is now an explicit 4.5%-of-sales fee to Meritor HVS India (Cummins) under a one-year agreement renewable 30-Apr-2027, structured below the shareholder-approval threshold after minority holders voted 79.5% against a Rs 2,500 cr material-RPT resolution in Dec-2024; (3, positive) the balance sheet is clean (net cash 15% of market cap, AA- ICRA, payout ~30%) and the business earned 15-22% ROIC across FY23-26, so the downside is a cyclical drawdown, not a solvency event. What would prove us wrong: FY27 revenue >= Rs 2,500 cr AND FY28 H1 revenue holding within 10% of H1 FY27 after the pre-buy (the cycle is longer than we assume), or a fee cut/stable fee with rising content per vehicle. Departure from the outside view: P(>=3x) far below the class (6% vs 21%) because a 3x needs ~25% EPS CAGR from a cyclical-peak base (twin engine); tail probabilities are anchored at w=0.6 toward the class because this stock already printed a ~0.2x drawdown in the last cycle. Checked by paper calls thesis:paper-call:AUTOAXLES:* (6 operating/fee/price calls to 2027-09-30, plus the 3 card calls). Open soft flags: 5. P(≥3x) 6% vs base 21%; P(≤0.5x) 4% vs base 11.3%; EV 5-yr multiple 1.49x vs hurdle 1.76x. Review 2027-02-15.
